title: Be a Chef
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for Shellfie.

pages: Today, you are a chef! A chef cooks food in a restaurant.
You wear a white jacket, an apron, and a tall white hat. Your shoes do not slip, because kitchen floors can be wet.
In the morning, you check the food that came in. Are the tomatoes red? Is the fish fresh? Then you chop, chop, chop.
You flip a pancake high in the air to show off. It goes up, up, up... and sticks to the ceiling!
Everyone waits. Plop! It lands right back in the pan. "I meant to do that," you say.
At dinner time, the kitchen gets very busy. This is called the dinner rush. Orders come in fast, and pots bubble everywhere.
You work with a team: other cooks, a helper chef called a sous chef, dishwashers, and servers who bring the food to the tables.
The best part? You make up new recipes, and you see people smile when they taste them.
The hardest part? The kitchen is hot, you stand all day, and you often work at night and on weekends.
How do you become a chef? Some chefs go to cooking school for 1 or 2 years. Others learn by working in a kitchen. Becoming the head chef can take 5 to 10 years.
What can you do now? Cook with a grown-up. Wash the veggies, stir the batter, and try a new food every week.

quiz.q: Why do chefs wear shoes that do not slip?
quiz.ev: Your shoes do not slip, because kitchen floors can be wet.
